providers.title: Ostmann's conjecture
providers.scope: If A and B are sets of nonnegative integers with at least two elements each, then the symmetric difference of A + B and the set of primes is infinite. Follows from Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 5.1 of lesson 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A sieve for finitely many shifts
providers.scope: If b_1, ..., b_j are distinct nonnegative integers and c + b_1, ..., c + b_j are all prime for every sufficiently large c in C, then C(Y) << Y/(log Y)^j for large Y, with an implied constant depending only on the shifts.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite summands (Laffer and Mann)
providers.scope: If A and B have at least two elements each and A + B is asymptotically equal to the set of primes, then A and B are infinite.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two infinite summands
providers.scope: There are no infinite sets A, B of nonnegative integers such that the symmetric difference of A + B and the set of primes is finite. Proved in lessons 2 to 18.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Square-root bounds (Elsholtz)
providers.scope: If A and B are infinite and the symmetric difference of A + B and the set of primes is finite, then sqrt(Y)/(log Y)^3 << A(Y), B(Y) << sqrt(Y)(log Y)^2 for Y >= 3.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Collision stability
providers.scope: For probability measures on the large elements of A and of -B with point masses at most (log X)^b/sqrt(X), the sum over primes p <= sqrt(X)/(log X)^(b+1) of log p times the squared L^2 distances of their reductions from the uniform measures on the residue support S_p and on its complement, plus (1/sigma_p + 1/(1 - sigma_p) - 4)/p, is O(log log X), and every term is nonnegative.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Decorrelation from translated quadratic characters
providers.scope: As T tends to infinity, the sum over primes with T <= log p <= 2T of (log p)/p times the maximum over t of |E_(x in S_p) chi_p(x - t)| is o(T), where chi_p is the quadratic character modulo p. Proved in lessons 3 to 6.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bonami's inequality for signs
providers.scope: For independent uniform random signs and F = sum over S of a_S prod_(i in S) eps_i with real coefficients, (E|F|^(2l))^(1/l) <= sum over S of (2l - 1)^|S| a_S^2 for every integer l >= 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Large quadratic Weyl sums
providers.scope: If a sum of e(alpha j^2 + beta j) over an interval of at most Y/c_1 integers has modulus at least c_1 Y e^(-K), with K large in terms of c_1, Y >= e^(4K) and log(2Y) <= e^K, then ||q alpha|| <= 2e^(8K)/Y^2 for some integer 1 <= q <= 2e^(8K).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A common rational centre
providers.scope: At least J Z^(-O(1/k)) of the J primes of a biased block have their translations t_p congruent to h/m modulo p, for one pair of coprime integers h, m with 1 <= m <= Z^0.13 and |h| <= X Z^0.15.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Heath-Brown's quadratic large sieve
providers.scope: For positive integers M, N, complex numbers a_n and eps > 0, the sum over odd squarefree m <= M of |sum over odd squarefree n <= N of a_n (n/m)|^2 is O_eps((MN)^eps (M + N) sum |a_n|^2). Used without proof, as named result N1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Split primes for a product of kernels
providers.scope: For the product vw of two small kernels, the primes p <= Q_2 = X^(1/2 - 5 eta) not dividing 2mvw with (vw/p) = 1 satisfy sum (log p)/p >= 0.03 log X; the proof uses the zero-free region with the exceptional zero and Siegel's theorem.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Decorrelation from characters of higher order
providers.scope: For fixed 0 < alpha < beta, the sum over primes with alpha L <= log log p <= beta L of (1/p) times the maximum over t and over characters lambda of order greater than two of |E_(x in S_p) lambda(x - t)| is o(L). Proved in lessons 7 to 9.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Kneser's addition theorem
providers.scope: For finite nonempty subsets A, B of an abelian group, |A + B| >= |A + K| + |B + K| - |K|, where K is the stabilizer of A + B (proof of DeVos). Corollary 3.3: a generating set U of a finite abelian group G with 0 in U and |U| >= rho|G| satisfies rU = G for every r >= 2/rho.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The transfer
providers.scope: Cauchy-Schwarz over the residues of the pivot, extended to positive integers, gives |eta_(j-1)|^2 <= e^(d_j)(eta_j + D_j), where D_j collects the diagonal terms and the off-diagonal part eta_j has the same form as eta_(j-1).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Uniqueness of frequency histories
providers.scope: For a fixed assignment of the top list and a fixed root frequency there is at most one valid history.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: One-sided character interactions
providers.scope: A factor xi_q(p), with xi_q a nonprincipal character modulo a short prime q and p a long prime, and with no factor in the reverse direction, makes the weighted expectation O(exp(-c e^(alpha L))).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Mixed flatness of the normalized transforms
providers.scope: Outside a set of primes of harmonic mass o(L) in the band alpha L <= log log p <= beta L, sigma_p = 1/2 + o(1) and the normalized transform g_p of the residue support has correlation o(1) with every product lambda(v) e_p(av) of a multiplicative and an additive character.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A supply of nonsparse transforms
providers.scope: There is an absolute delta_0 > 0 such that for large L the primes with 0.05 L <= log log p <= 0.9 L, 1/3 <= sigma_p <= 2/3 and gamma_p >= delta_0, where gamma_p is the probability L^1 norm of g_p, satisfy sum 1/p >= 0.15 L. Proved in lessons 10 and 11 from the sieve estimates and coverage.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A contracting local kernel
providers.scope: For a balanced prime whose transform is sparse (gamma_p < delta_0), the kernel built from the large Fourier coefficients of the support, written in block coordinates between the support and its complement, has norm at most (1 - 1.6/p) times its mean U_p(1,1) = 1 + O(eps_0/p) over the nonzero residues.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Prime sums twisted by a family of characters
providers.scope: For every fixed D_1 > 0, the sum over primitive characters chi of conductor at most Q_b, without the exceptional character, of |sum Lambda(n) chi(n) phi(n/X) - 1_(chi=1) X Phi(1)| is O(X e^(-D_1 L)); the proof uses the explicit formula, the zero-free region and the log-free zero-density estimate.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The tree comparison over a finite field
providers.scope: A single binary-tree diagram of transforms over F_q with independent uniform leaf variables has E|W|^2 <= 3^r. For two diagrams of depth l >= 2 whose r leaves are partitioned into b <= 3r/4 paired blocks, with leaf variables uniform subject to equal products over paired blocks, |E W_1 conj(W_2)| <= C_l(eps_q + q^(-1/4)). Proved in lessons 12 and 13.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A uniform Mellin estimate
providers.scope: For every multiplicative character eta and every a in F_q, the sum over all multiplicative characters chi of the squared Fourier coefficient at a of P_chi chi eta, where P_chi are the Mellin coefficients of a bottom-pair autocorrelation, is at most q/(q - 1)(eps_q^4 + sqrt(3) q^(-1/2)); each nonidentity affine map of F_q arises in at most two ways.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The exact transfer
providers.scope: For 1 <= j <= k, e^(-c_g)|eta_(j-1)|^2 <= D_j + eta_j, with a nonnegative diagonal D_j and a real eta_j.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The comparison estimates
providers.scope: For one assignment, the weighted mean square of the depth-l amplitude is at most exp(r(Delta_0 + Cm) + o_k(m)); for two assignments with l >= 2 whose overlap graph has at most 3r/4 components, the weighted correlation is at most exp(-omega_k(m)) with omega_k(m)/m tending to infinity. Proved in lessons 15 to 17.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Primes in progressions in short logarithmic intervals
providers.scope: For log M_* <= e^(mu L), a residue a coprime to M_* and an interval I of length at most 1 inside [e^(a_0 L), e^(a_1 L)], the sum of 1/p over primes p = a mod M_* with log p in I equals 1/phi(M_*) times the integral over I of (1 - chi_*(a) e^((beta_* - 1)t)) dt/t, up to O(exp(-c e^(delta' L))), where chi_* is the possible exceptional real character and beta_* its real zero.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The signed comparison
providers.scope: Under the hypotheses of the pair estimate of lesson 14, the weighted correlation of two assignments is at most eps_k(L)^m exp(O_k(m)) + O(exp(-e^(0.00125 L))) = exp(-omega_k(m)), from the tree comparison at every spectator prime.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The norm comparison
providers.scope: Under the hypotheses of the norm estimate of lesson 14, the weighted mean square of the depth-l amplitude is at most exp(r(Delta_0 + Cm) + o_k(m)), with C independent of large k and of the gap constants.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The lower bound
providers.scope: For large L, -log|eta_j| <= 2^j B_* m + (2^j - 1)(c_g + log 2) < B 2^j m for 0 <= j <= k.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The norm of the common regular transform
providers.scope: For large L, the expectation of the sum over 0 < |s| <= V_k of |G_R(s/d)|^2 is O(V_k) with an absolute implied constant.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
